kicker: Battery storage · demand vs Indian cell supply
title: India's storage boom still runs on imported cells
dek: Storage could reach about 302 GWh by FY32 from 6.3 GWh in FY26 (industry estimate). ACME's ~19 GWh of batteries on order are all Chinese, Amara Raja still imports ~70% of its cells and Indian cells cost 5–15% more.

read: Until a local-content rule or incentive closes the 5–15% gap, the first wave of Indian storage will be built on Chinese cells.
sources: Vantage analysis of Q1–Q2 FY27 earnings calls of ACME Solar, Exide Industries, Amara Raja and Waaree Energies; industry estimates; Vantage sector intel, 21 Nov 2026
notes: The FY32 storage figure (302 GWh, from 6.3 GWh in FY26) and the ~90% import share are industry estimates, not company data. Demand columns are from ACME's Q2 FY27 call: about 19 GWh of batteries contracted with CATL, Hithium, Ganfeng, Trina and CLOU; FY27 commissioning target raised to over 12 GWh; and SECI's 4 GW / 16 GWh peak-power auction. Cell columns: Exide's 6 GWh lithium-ion plant was commissioned on 23 September 2026, but its large-format storage-cell line waits on incentive clarity; Amara Raja's 5 GWh LFP cell plant was approved this quarter with about 30 months to build; Waaree's 3.5 GWh cell pilot is due from Q4 FY27 and its 16.5 GWh second phase is in planning, with funding tied to policy. Cost gaps are on a landed basis as stated by management; ACME's call describes the January change as a 6% Chinese export tax, Exide's as the end of a 6% export rebate.
